title: leggedrobotics/pace-sim2real
summary: PACE targets sim-to-real transfer for legged robots by systematically identifying actuator and joint dynamics using only standard joint encoder measurements. The repository appears focused on making simulation models better match real robot behavior without extra sensing hardware, which is useful for deploying learned locomotion policies with fewer reality-gap surprises.

It is aimed at robot learning workflows where fast iteration, scalable reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer matter, using MuJoCo as the physics backbone.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for writing GPU-accelerated simulation and differentiable computation code, aimed at robotics, graphics, and machine learning workloads. It is useful when you need custom physics, geometry, or numerical kernels that run efficiently on CUDA while staying accessible from Python workflows.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a lightweight sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and reinforcement learning agents without depending on ROS. It provides native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution across several common robot platforms, including Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101, making it useful for researchers who want a leaner path from simulation experiments to real robot control.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable setup for building and scaling robotics simulation environments. It is aimed at quickly prototyping and evaluating robot learning policies across different robot embodiments, objects, and task environments, making it useful for stress-testing policies beyond a single fixed simulator setup.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: XuPeng23/AeroVLA
summary: AeroVLA is an ECCV 2026 vision-language-action model for UAV navigation that maps visual and language inputs directly to minimalist end-to-end control actions. The repository appears to provide the official implementation for training or evaluating this aerial navigation policy, with interest mainly in how far VLA-style embodied control can be simplified for drones without hand-engineered planning stacks.

extra.full_text: [Accepted to ECCV 2026] Official repository for AeroVLA (formerly known as AerialVLA): A Vision-Language-Action Model for UAV Navigation via Minimalist End-to-End Control

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for training and testing basic quadruped locomotion, with support for multiple robot platforms rather than a single fixed morphology. It is aimed at practical policy development workflows, including sim-to-sim transfer and sim-to-real deployment, so it is useful as a starting point for researchers who want a compact locomotion environment that connects simulation training to real robot experiments.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse
summary: RoboVerse aims to unify robot learning infrastructure by packaging a platform, dataset, and benchmark around scalable, generalizable robot behavior. title: iLearn-Lab/CVPR26-OptimusVLA
summary: OptimusVLA is the official implementation of a CVPR 2026 vision-language-action model for robotic manipulation that combines a global prior with local consistency through a dual-memory design. The interesting part is the memory mechanism: it augments action generation with broader task-level context while preserving locally coherent manipulation behavior, aiming to make robot control more efficient and reliable.
